prompt: Stage 2-5, level 5, 88 HP after two close losses. You just combined two defensive components into a completed tank item. Your front line is a 2-star 1-cost tank in the centre, a 2-star bruiser beside him, and a 1-star 2-cost tank you bought this round on the flank. Who holds it?
explanation:
A defensive item goes on the unit that gets hit first, and that is the 2-star 1-cost tank in the centre of the front row: enemies walk to the closest unit, and the centre-front is closest for the whole enemy team. A 2-star with a completed item at 2-5 holds the line long enough for your carry to kill things, which turns close losses into wins. The item is on the board, working, from this fight on.

The temptation is the 2-cost tank: higher cost, 'he will be my real tank later'. He is 1-star and on the flank, so the item would sit on a unit that is hit second and dies first. Later is later: when the 2-cost becomes 2-star and moves to the centre, the item can move too, and by then you will have more. The bruiser is the wrong shape: he is beside the tank, not in front of the enemy path. The carry does not want a defensive item at all. Slam on the front unit you have.
principle: The tank item goes on the unit that takes the first hits today, not on the unit you hope will take them later.
commonMistake: Holding the tank item for the 'real' tank, or putting it on the higher-cost 1-star on the flank while the 2-star in the centre dies naked.
hint: Look at which unit the enemy reaches first and which of the frontliners is a 2-star. Later upgrades can inherit the item.
